title: State of AI Regulation
dek_2026: AI law and policy counted: what the EU, the US federal government, the US states, China and the UK have enacted, delayed and enforced, with every count dated and sourced.

2024: The EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) entered into force on 1 August 2024, with fines of up to €35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited practices under Article 99.
MultiState counted 635 AI-related bills introduced in US state legislatures in 2024, of which 99 were enacted.
Stanford HAI's AI Index 2025 counted 131 AI-related state laws passed in the United States in 2024, up from 49 in 2023, and 59 AI-related federal agency regulations, up from 25.
Stanford HAI's AI Index 2025 found that mentions of AI in the legislative proceedings of 75 countries rose 21.3% in 2024, to 1,889 from 1,557 in 2023.
China ended 2024 with 302 generative-AI services filed with the Cyberspace Administration of China, according to CAC filing data reported by legal trackers.
2025: The EU AI Act's bans on prohibited practices applied from 2 February 2025 and its obligations for general-purpose AI models from 2 August 2025, according to the European Commission's timeline.
MultiState counted 1,208 AI-related bills introduced in US state legislatures in 2025 and 145 enacted, while NCSL's count for the same year is 1,262 introduced and 227 enacted.
The US Senate voted 99–1 in July 2025 to strip a proposed 10-year moratorium on state AI regulation from the federal budget bill.
President Trump signed Executive Order 14365 on 11 December 2025, directing the Attorney General to set up an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws.
China's mandatory labelling rules for AI-generated content took effect on 1 September 2025, and 748 generative-AI services had completed CAC filing by the end of 2025, 446 of them during the year.
2026: The EU's AI Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026, moved the AI Act's stand-alone high-risk obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 and adds two Article 5 prohibitions, including 'nudifier' apps, from 2 December 2026.
NCSL counted 1,539 AI bills introduced and 280 enacted in US state legislatures in 2026 as of early October 2026.

Reps. Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced the AI Kill Switch Act on 23 July 2026, proposing fines of up to $20 million a day for defying a federal shutdown order; it had not advanced by November 2026.
Public Citizen counted 31 US states with election-deepfake laws in October 2026, while roughly 45–48 states have laws addressing sexual deepfakes.
No fine under the EU AI Act had been published as of late September 2026, although the European Commission's power to fine general-purpose AI providers began on 2 August 2026.

2024: 2024 was the year AI law moved from proposal to statute, almost entirely outside Washington. The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, though none of its obligations applied before 2025; its significance that year was the penalty ceiling it fixed, €35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover, and the staged calendar it set. In the United States the activity was in the states: MultiState counted 635 AI bills introduced and 99 enacted, and Stanford HAI's AI Index counted 131 state AI laws passed, up from 49 in 2023. The two numbers differ because the trackers define an AI law differently, a problem that runs through every year of this series.

Federal policy in 2024 ran through agencies and memoranda rather than statute or new executive orders. Stanford HAI counted 59 AI-related federal regulations in 2024, more than double the 25 of 2023, issued by 42 agencies. The Biden order EO 14110 remained the federal framework until January 2025, and California's sweeping frontier bill SB 1047 was vetoed in September 2024, which set the ceiling for how far US frontier-model regulation would go. Enforcement was narrow and case-by-case: the FCC's $6 million fine over an AI-cloned Biden robocall is the clearest example of an existing regulator applying old law to synthetic media.

China and the rest of the world followed their own paths. China regulated through three CAC administrative rules (on recommendation algorithms, deep synthesis and generative-AI services) and ended the year with 302 generative-AI services filed with the regulator. The UK kept its principles-based approach with no statute. Across 75 countries, Stanford HAI counted 1,889 mentions of AI in legislative proceedings in 2024, up 21.3% in a year, and 40 AI-related laws passed nationally. The overall picture at the end of 2024 was one binding comprehensive regime, the EU's, that had not yet begun to apply.
2025: In 2025 the EU AI Act began to apply. Prohibitions and AI-literacy duties took effect on 2 February 2025 and obligations for general-purpose AI models on 2 August 2025, when 26 providers signed the GPAI Code of Practice and Meta declined. The calendar also started to slip. On 19 November 2025 the Commission proposed the Digital Omnibus, which would move the stand-alone high-risk obligations from August 2026 to December 2027. No AI Act fine was issued during the year. The EU's main AI enforcement came under data-protection law instead, including Italy's €5 million fine on Replika's developer.

US federal policy turned deregulatory and then took on the states. EO 14179 in January replaced the Biden framework, the AI Action Plan and three executive orders followed in July, and by our count eight AI-focused executive orders were signed in 2025. Congress tried to freeze state law: a 10-year moratorium was struck from the budget bill by 99–1 in July. The White House then acted on its own with EO 14365 on 11 December, which ordered an AI Litigation Task Force and tied federal broadband funds to state AI laws. The year's one significant AI-specific federal statute was the TAKE IT DOWN Act, signed in May.

The states kept legislating. MultiState counted 1,208 AI bills introduced and 145 enacted, and NCSL later put the year at 1,262 and 227. California enacted SB 53, the first US frontier-model transparency law, and Texas enacted TRAIGA. Colorado delayed its first-in-the-nation AI Act to June 2026. Election-deepfake laws passed 25 states by mid-year. China added mandatory labelling of AI content from 1 September and nearly tripled its stock of filed generative-AI services, from 302 to 748. Japan's non-punitive AI Promotion Act took effect, so two of the nine jurisdictions we map had an AI-specific statute in force.
2026: The defining EU event of 2026 was a delay. The AI Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, has been in force since 27 July 2026. It moved stand-alone high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and product-embedded systems to 2 August 2028, and it added two Article 5 prohibitions, including 'nudifier' apps, that apply from 2 December 2026. Some duties did go live on schedule: the Article 50 transparency rules, and the Commission's power to fine general-purpose AI providers, both from 2 August 2026. As of late September 2026 no AI Act fine had been published. On paper the EU's penalties are still the world's highest, but the regime has not yet produced a fine.

In the US, federal action stayed executive and largely deregulatory. EO 14409 was signed on 2 June 2026, and the bipartisan Great American AI Act, which would preempt state AI laws for three years, remains a discussion draft. The DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, set up on 9 January 2026, has mainly intervened in xAI's challenge to Colorado's law rather than bringing suits of its own. The one new safety proposal was the AI Kill Switch Act of 23 July 2026, which followed an OpenAI model's reported breach of Hugging Face. Its $20 million-a-day penalty has drawn attention, but we estimate its chance of becoming law as written this Congress at about 5%.

The states kept legislating despite the federal pressure. NCSL counted 1,539 AI bills introduced and 280 enacted by early October 2026, already more enactments than its count for all of 2025. Few of these are broad frameworks. Only Colorado's SB 26-189, which replaced the 2024 Act with a narrower disclosure model effective January 2027, and Connecticut's SB 5 count as broad governance laws. Most of the rest deal with chatbots, minors, employment and deepfakes. Public Citizen counted 31 states with election-deepfake laws in October 2026, while 45–48 states address sexual deepfakes, and the federal TAKE IT DOWN removal duty has been enforced by the FTC since 19 May 2026.

Outside the EU and the US, statute-making stayed slow while administrative control grew. China has no national AI law, but its CAC filing regime reached 1,112 generative-AI services and 731 registered apps by 31 August 2026. South Korea's AI Basic Act took effect on 22 January 2026, so three of the nine jurisdictions we map now have an AI-specific statute in force. The UK still has no AI statute; its October 2026 package added AI incident reporting under a cyber-security bill. Enforcement remained thin. The largest EU generative-AI privacy fine, Italy's €15 million against OpenAI, was annulled by the Court of Rome in March 2026.

takeaways_2026: The EU slowed down instead of tightening: the AI Omnibus (in force 27 July 2026) moved stand-alone high-risk duties to 2 December 2027, and no AI Act fine had been published as of late September 2026.
US states enacted 280 AI bills by early October 2026 (NCSL), more than NCSL's full-year 2025 count of 227, despite the federal preemption push in EO 14365 and the DOJ AI Litigation Task Force.
There is still no comprehensive US federal AI statute: the Great American AI Act is a discussion draft and the AI Kill Switch Act (23 July 2026) has not advanced.
China grows its filing regime instead of passing a single AI law: 1,112 generative-AI services filed with the CAC by 31 August 2026, up from 302 at the end of 2024.
yoy_takeaways: US state AI lawmaking roughly doubled each year on MultiState's count from 2024 to 2025 (635 to 1,208 bills introduced; 99 to 145 enacted), and NCSL's 2026 year-to-date enactments (280) already exceed its 2025 total (227). Different trackers give different totals, so compare within one tracker only.
EU AI Act deadlines moved later each year: in 2024 stand-alone high-risk duties were due on 2 August 2026, a delay to December 2027 was proposed in 2025, and the Omnibus made it law in 2026.

US federal policy went from agency rule-making in 2024 (59 regulations) to executive orders in 2025 (eight by our count, ending with EO 14365 against state AI laws) and to proposals in 2026 (EO 14409, the Great American AI Act draft and the AI Kill Switch Act), with no comprehensive statute in any of the three years.

China's filed generative-AI services went from 302 at the end of 2024 to 748 at the end of 2025 and 1,112 by 31 August 2026. Its binding AI-specific rules went from three to four, with labelling added in September 2025.

faq_2026.q: Does the United States have a federal AI law in 2026?
faq_2026.a: No comprehensive one. As of November 2026 US federal AI policy runs through executive orders, most recently EO 14409 of 2 June 2026, and EO 14365 of 11 December 2025, which set up a DOJ task force to challenge state AI laws. The bipartisan Great American AI Act, which would preempt state laws for three years, is still a discussion draft. The AI Kill Switch Act, introduced on 23 July 2026, has not advanced. The main AI-specific federal statute in force is the TAKE IT DOWN Act of May 2025 on nonconsensual intimate imagery.

faq_2026.q: When do the EU AI Act's high-risk rules apply now?
faq_2026.a: Under the AI Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026, obligations for stand-alone high-risk systems listed in Annex III apply from 2 December 2027 instead of 2 August 2026. High-risk AI embedded in regulated products follows on 2 August 2028. Article 50 transparency duties and the Commission's fining power over general-purpose AI providers applied from 2 August 2026, and two new Article 5 prohibitions, including 'nudifier' apps, apply from 2 December 2026.

faq_2026.q: How many AI bills have US states passed in 2026?
faq_2026.a: NCSL counted 280 AI bills enacted out of 1,539 introduced in US state legislatures in 2026 as of early October 2026, more than its count of 227 enacted in all of 2025. Other trackers count differently: ailawsbystate.com listed 252 enacted by 5 October 2026, and the Transparency Coalition 115 laws in 30 states between 1 January and 15 October 2026. Only two were broad governance laws, Colorado's SB 26-189 and Connecticut's SB 5.

faq_2026.q: How many US states have deepfake laws?
faq_2026.a: It depends on the type. Public Citizen counted 31 states with election-deepfake laws in October 2026, and trackers range from 30 to 33. Laws addressing sexual deepfakes exist in roughly 45–48 states. Quoting '45 states' for election protection overstates it. Most election-deepfake laws require a disclosure label rather than banning the content, and some have been blocked in court.

faq_2026.q: Has anyone been fined under the EU AI Act?
faq_2026.a: Not as of late September 2026, according to law-firm and tracker reporting; neither the European Commission nor any national authority had published an AI Act fine. The Commission's power to fine general-purpose AI providers (up to €15 million or 3% of turnover) began on 2 August 2026. EU enforcement against AI chatbots has come under data-protection law instead, such as Italy's €158,000 fine on Character.AI in July 2026. The largest such fine, €15 million against OpenAI, was annulled in March 2026.
